format: Each front end of the engine (architecture/engine.md, Parity), and the manifest it published at a pinned commit, as a file in checks/front-ends/: the CLI's is `weblisk commands --json`, Studio's is GET /api/operations, both the engine's one manifest (ops.Catalogue) at the engine the commit builds against. `executors` holds the --parity leg to the operations of those executors in the catalogue and in each manifest: S1 is done for local and tenant-api (ENGINE_PLAN, Order). `expected_gaps` is what the leg finds, measured, and is held exactly: a gap that closes leaves the list, a new one fails. Every gap today is the engine's, and `gap_reasons` says why each is open, by operation; each closes in the engine (E2 to E4, T1), not in a front end. Since manifest_version 3 an entry is architecture/engine's (operation, executor, capability, parameters, events, records). A front end with no manifest makes checks/front-end-parity.py --parity NOT RUN, never ok.

gap_reasons.change plan: cli-in-tenant until a tenant runs its change service (ENGINE_PLAN T1): the act runs on the tenant's own host, and labelling it tenant-api would send a client to routes no tenant serves yet (architecture/cli, Until a tenant runs a change service). The engine lists it as cli-in-tenant, which the leg's executors leave out.
gap_reasons.change list: cli-in-tenant until a tenant runs its change service (ENGINE_PLAN T1): the act runs on the tenant's own host, and labelling it tenant-api would send a client to routes no tenant serves yet (architecture/cli, Until a tenant runs a change service). The engine lists it as cli-in-tenant, which the leg's executors leave out.

The engine lists it as cli-in-tenant, which the leg's executors leave out.
gap_reasons.change apply: cli-in-tenant until a tenant runs its change service (ENGINE_PLAN T1): the act runs on the tenant's own host, and labelling it tenant-api would send a client to routes no tenant serves yet (architecture/cli, Until a tenant runs a change service). The engine lists it as cli-in-tenant, which the leg's executors leave out.
gap_reasons.change verify: not built: until the change service runs (T1) the tools refuse it by name; verify is a build run in the tenant (architecture/change-service).
gap_reasons.change revert: not built: until the change service runs (T1) the tools refuse it by name; a revert is a change plan of kind revert (architecture/change-service).
gap_reasons.cache status: cli-in-tenant until T1: the generation cache is the tenant host's, where change apply runs today; the catalogue's local cache is the one a client keeps once builds run in the tenant.
gap_reasons.cache prune: cli-in-tenant until T1, as cache status.
gap_reasons.build: no engine entry yet: a scratch build outside any tenant (architecture/engine, The build steps) needs the steps to run without a tenant directory, which E2 to E4 build.
gap_reasons.programme adopt: no engine code yet: adopting a programme is still Studio's own flow over the content service, and moves into the engine with the change service (T1).
gap_reasons.standard adopt: no engine code yet: adopting a standard is still Studio's own flow over the content service, and moves into the engine with the change service (T1).
